Note::overlap_tokens¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::overlap_tokens(const Note& other) const

Word-Set Containment Score Between Two Notes¶

overlap_tokens(other) reduces each cell of self and the matching cell of other to a set of words and returns their overlap coefficient — the size of the intersection divided by the size of the smaller set — as a shape-preserving Note of score strings. It is the word-level containment member of the set-similarity family, next to jaccard_tokens (a mutual-similarity score) and intersect_tokens (which returns the shared words).

How the score is computed¶

Each cell is tokenized with the ASCII word tokenizer (as tokenize_words does), lowercased, and deduplicated into sets A (from self) and B (from other). The score is

|A ∩ B| / min(|A|, |B|)

a value in [0, 1], symmetric.

The key property: the score is 1.0 whenever the smaller set is entirely contained in the larger one, no matter how much bigger the larger set is. So overlap_tokens answers “is one cell’s vocabulary a subset of the other’s?” rather than “how similar are the two vocabularies?” — for the latter, use jaccard_tokens, where the extra words in the larger set lower the score.

Edge cases¶

  • Both sets empty → "1.0".

  • One set empty, the other not → "0.0" (the smaller size is 0).

Result shape and formatting¶

The result is a Note with the same shape as the pairing’s non-scalar side. Each score is formatted with up to six decimal places, trailing zeros trimmed, always at least one digit after the point ("1.0", "0.666667").

Shape, pairing, and rejections¶

Per cell and pairwise; equal numel or a scalar (numel() == 1) broadcast. Rejections raise pluss::Error:

  • either side in bytes mode → Note::overlap_tokens requires a UTF-8 text Note (lhs is bytes) (or rhs is bytes).

  • unequal numel with neither side a scalar → Note::overlap_tokens expects equal numel or scalar broadcast.

Example 1: A Subset Scores 1.0¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"quick brown fox"})
                 .overlap_tokens(pluss::make_note({"the quick brown fox jumps over"}))
          << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["1.0"]

Every word of the smaller set {quick, brown, fox} is in the larger set, so the coefficient is 1.0. jaccard_tokens on the same pair would give 3/6 = 0.5.

Example 2: A Genuine Partial Overlap¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"a b c d"})
                 .overlap_tokens(pluss::make_note({"c d e"}))
          << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["0.666667"]

Sets {a, b, c, d} and {c, d, e} share two words; the smaller set has three → 2/3.

Example 3: Disjoint And One-Empty¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"a b"}).overlap_tokens(pluss::make_note({"c d"})) << "\n";
std::cout << pluss::make_note({"a b"}).overlap_tokens(pluss::make_note({""})) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["0.0"]
Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["0.0"]

See Also¶

  • Note::jaccard_tokens: |A ∩ B| / |A ∪ B| — size differences lower the score.

  • Note::intersect_tokens: the shared words, not a score.

  • Note::overlap_terms: the same score over content words only.
